From: Amy Ho <amy.ho@heliumhealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.example, ben_carter@redwood.example
Cc: LegalOps <legalops@heliumhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 13:12:00 +0000
Subject: Data terms: proposed edits and questions

Hi Karthik / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — product looks promising. Our legal team did a first pass on the MSA + Order Form and produced a redline focused on the DPA / transfer clauses (SCCs and processor roles). I'm attaching the redline (HeliumHealth_DPA_Redlines_20261201.docx).

Top-level asks from our side:
- Clarify controller vs processor responsibilities in Section 3 (we think some operational obligations still read like controller obligations).
- Add explicit KMS options and a commitment on key custody for EU patient data (we prefer KMS with customer-managed keys or an approved HSM workflow).
- For SCCs: Helium wants to ensure the latest 2024/2025 standard contractual clauses are adopted and any transfer addendum references the specific module used.
- Request a timeline for evidence (SOC2, encryption-at-rest, subprocessor list) ahead of signature.

Can Redwood confirm whether private deployment (VPC) will be an available option for the pilot? If so, we'd like rough lead times and any additional costs surfaced now.

We'd prefer a short call to walk through the redline and align on a plan for legal + procurement. Are you available tomorrow afternoon?

Thanks — attaching the redline.

Best,
Amy Ho
Head of Contracts (on behalf of LegalOps)
Helium Health

Attachment: HeliumHealth_DPA_Redlines_20261201.docx (redline, ~12 pages)

Amy — thanks for sending the redline and the clear notes. We appreciate the level of detail.

Quick responses:
- Private deployment (VPC): yes — we can offer a VPC-hosted private deployment for the pilot. Typical lead time is 6–8 weeks from PO + infra kickoff; there may be a one-time onboarding fee. Ben, can you confirm the commercial estimate?
- KMS / key custody: we support both Redwood-managed keys and customer-managed KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK) depending on the deployment. For VPC/private customers we can scope customer-managed keys + HSM.
- SCCs: we use the latest EU SCCs and can reference the exact module in the transfer addendum. Laura, legal, can you flag anything in their redline that would block standard SCC adoption?

Suggested next steps:
1) Quick triage call (30 min) with Amy + Helium legal, Ben, Laura, and myself tomorrow 15:00 UTC to walk the redline and confirm the non-starters.
2) Redwood legal to provide a short annotated summary of Helium's redline and our proposed alternatives within 48 hours of the call.
3) If there are delegation/processor questions, produce a one‑page responsibilities matrix for signature with the Order Form.

Amy — does 15:00 UTC tomorrow work? If not, propose one other slot tomorrow afternoon your side.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Legal Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.example <laura_bennett@redwood.example>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.example, ben_carter@redwood.example
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 08:00:00 +0000
Subject: Internal: Helium redline — quick read and recommendations

Folks — I reviewed Helium's redline (attached) and pulled the items I think require an executive/legal decision vs those we can accept or counter locally. Key notes: 

1) Controller/Processor split 
- Their edits widen Helium's controller obligations in Section 3. We should push back on operational obligations that would force Redwood to accept primary liability for data collection practices. Proposed language: narrow obligations to processing on behalf of the controller; add a carveout for actions required by law enforcement.

2) KMS and key custody
- For hosted customers we offer Redwood-managed keys only; for Dedicated/Private we can support customer-managed KMS. Helium is requesting CMK for pilot that includes EU patient data — recommend accepting for VPC/pilot but require an onboarding security review and a one-time engineering fee.

3) SCCs / transfer addendum
- We can adopt the latest SCCs but Helium insists on naming the module and attaching a transfer addendum. Recommend: attach SCC module 2 (controller-processor) and include a schedule naming the module and execution date.

4) Subprocessor list and evidence
- We can provide SOC2 report and encryption details within our standard evidence package, but subprocessor disclosure cadence (they ask monthly) is excessive. Recommend weekly for pilot or on-request with 5 business days SLA.

5) Indemnity/liability caps
- Helium redlines include a higher carveout for regulatory fines tied to transfers. Recommend we keep standard caps but expand exclusions where Redwood can demonstrate compliance actions were taken.

Actionable ask for Ben/Karthik:
- Ben: confirm commercial impact (VPC onboarding fee, lead time) so I can include that in our annotated response.
- Karthik: please confirm if we are prepared to accept naming SCC module 2 and attaching a transfer addendum as a path to signature.

I'll prepare a one-page annotated summary (RH_internal_summary_DPA_notes_20261202.pdf) with tracked suggested language and cut/paste alternatives for the call.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: RH_internal_summary_DPA_notes_20261202.pdf (internal summary)

Subject: RE: Data terms: proposed edits and questions — proposed path forward

Hi Amy / Helium legal team — thanks for the detailed redline and for the call earlier today. Karthik and Laura have reviewed and we've agreed the following proposed path forward to keep timetable tight for the pilot: 

1) SCCs: Redwood will accept attaching the EU SCCs (controller-processor module) and will sign the transfer addendum referencing the current module. We'll supply the executed module in the final contract packet.

2) KMS: For the pilot we can provision a VPC/private deployment with customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS) under an onboarding plan. There will be a one-time engineering onboarding fee of $18,000 and an estimated lead time of 6 weeks from P.O. to production readiness.

3) Evidence: Redwood will provide SOC 2 Type II and an encryption whitepaper within 7 business days of a signed NDA. Subprocessor list will be provided on-request within 5 business days for the pilot.

4) Controller/Processor language: Redwood accepts narrowing Section 3 to processing on behalf of the controller; we will provide suggested text via the annotated summary Laura is drafting.

5) Next steps and timing: Laura will send the annotated redline within 48 hours (internal summary attached). If Helium accepts, we can exchange signature-ready docs via DocuSign the following week. HubSpot deal updated: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/83421

If this captures it, please confirm and we'll follow up with the redline we propose.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
